article.title: が como sujeto focal
article.part: Arquitectura básica de la oración — 文の基本構造
article.chapter: Tópico, sujeto y contraste: は/が — 主題・主語・対比：は／が

claims.summary: Vermeulen (2012) presents a Japanese constituent question dare-ga wain-o nonda no? and an answer Taro-ga wain-o nonda, marking the answer constituent Taro-ga as focus; the question-answer context identifies the requested subject.

The focus reading is identified by the wh-question and its answer context; Yoshimoto (1982) describes ga as marking the syntactic relation between an NP and predicate and distinguishes this from information-structural effects, so ga is not described as a universal standalone emphasis marker.

Vermeulen (2012) notes that complete-sentence answers shown in the example are somewhat awkward because given material is preferably unpronounced; the answer constituent alone or a reduced response is more natural.
